title: Chandramana Yugadi
subtitle: Chandramana New Year
description: Chandramana Yugadi marks the beginning of the lunar year. In the Madhwa tradition, Panchanga puja and Panchanga shravana give the day its distinctive devotional focus.
notes: Begin with the household worship followed in your family, then Panchanga puja and Panchanga shravana.
Offer and share bevu-bella, the neem-and-jaggery preparation associated with accepting the year's mixed experiences.
Temple darshana, respect to elders, and the local Matha programme complete the day; follow their prescribed timings.

title: Sri Ramanavami
subtitle: Commemoration of Sri Rama
description: Sri Ramanavami commemorates the birth of Sri Rama on Chaitra Shukla Navami. Madhwa practice centres Sri Rama worship within the day's regular devotional discipline.
notes: Where followed at home, perform Saligrama puja before Sri Rama puja.
A simple home observance may use a Sri Rama picture, a clean worship space, customary offerings, and arati.
Join the temple programme or Ramayana recitation where available; follow the Matha for the complete ritual sequence.

title: Akshaya Tritiya
subtitle: Auspicious Vaishakha Tritiya
description: Akshaya Tritiya is observed as an auspicious spring tithi. The word akshaya expresses what is enduring or undiminished, and many households mark the day through worship and charity.
notes: Begin with prayer at home or at the temple.
Acts of dana and service are widely associated with the day.
For rites or vows, follow the published Matha and family tradition.

title: Narasimha Jayanti
subtitle: Sri Narasimha appearance day
description: Narasimha Jayanti commemorates Sri Vishnu's Narasimha avatara and the protection of Prahlada. It is especially important in Vaishnava practice across South India.
notes: Attend Lakshmi Narasimha or Vishnu temple worship where available.
Reading or listening to Prahlada's account is a traditional devotional practice.
Fasting customs vary; observe only according to family, health, and Matha guidance.

title: Naga Chaturthi
subtitle: Naga worship observance
description: Naga Chaturthi is observed in the Shravan season with regional traditions of reverence for the Nagas. Customs vary substantially by family and locality.
notes: Follow the observance followed by your family or local temple.
Avoid substituting general online instructions for a local religious programme.

title: Naga Panchami
subtitle: Naga worship observance
description: Naga Panchami is a Hindu observance dedicated to the Nagas and is marked by regional forms of worship, prayer, and offerings.
notes: Attend the local temple observance if one is held.
Follow the practice prescribed by family and local tradition.

title: Sri Krishna Janmashtami
subtitle: Commemoration of Sri Krishna's birth
description: Sri Krishna Janmashtami commemorates the birth of Sri Krishna. Vaishnava observance commonly includes worship, devotional singing, scripture recitation, fasting, and a night programme.
notes: Attend the temple's Janmashtami puja and follow its published timing.
Bhagavata Purana or Bhagavad Gita recitation and bhajans are common devotional practices.
Fasting and its conclusion vary by tradition; follow the Matha programme.

title: Sharannavaratri Aarambha
subtitle: Beginning of Sharad Navaratri
description: Sharad Navaratri begins a nine-night period of worship in many Hindu traditions. Regional forms, deities, and temple programmes differ, so the published local schedule should guide observance.
notes: Begin with the temple or household sankalpa followed in your tradition.
Attend the daily puja, discourse, or cultural programme where available.
Follow the local temple's sequence for each day of Navaratri.

title: Vijayadashami
subtitle: Vijaya Dashami / Dasara
description: Vijayadashami concludes Navaratri and is widely understood as a celebration of the victory of dharma over adharma. In Karnataka it is also known as Dasara.
notes: Attend the closing temple worship and procession where one is held.
Many households offer respect to books, tools, and instruments as part of the season's learning and work traditions.
Regional rites vary; follow the local temple programme.

title: Deepavali Amavasya
subtitle: Deepavali new-moon observance
description: Deepavali Amavasya is the principal new-moon night of Deepavali. Homes and temples are illuminated with lamps, while the precise puja sequence varies by sampradaya and place.
notes: Light lamps and attend the temple's published Deepavali puja where possible.
Families commonly clean and decorate the home, pray, and share food together.
Follow the SRS Matha programme for any specific observance or timing.

title: Utthana Dvadashi
subtitle: Kartika Shukla Dvadashi
description: Utthana Dvadashi is observed in Kartika Shukla Paksha and marks the close of Chaturmasya vrata. In Madhwa practice, it is closely associated with the Tulasi and Sri Krishna observance held that evening.
notes: Follow the morning worship and the local temple's Dvadashi timing.
The evening observance commonly prepares for Tulasi Vivaha with offerings, lamps, and devotion to Sri Krishna and Tulasi.
Use the SRS Matha programme for the complete procedure and any fasting or parana instruction.

title: Tulasi Vivaha
subtitle: Tulasi marriage observance
description: Tulasi Vivaha is the Kartika ceremonial observance of Tulasi and Sri Krishna, held with Utthana Dvadashi in the Madhwa tradition. It is a household and temple celebration with a detailed local ritual form.
notes: Complete the morning worship, then prepare the evening naivedya according to family practice.
Decorate the Tulasi brindavana, place a Sri Krishna image or icon there, and light lamps for the ceremony.
Use the SRS Matha or family procedure for sankalpa, offerings, and the complete Vivaha sequence.

title: Makara Sankramana
subtitle: Solar transition into Makara
description: Makara Sankramana marks the Sun's transition into Makara. It is observed across India with regional names, harvest customs, worship, and charity.
notes: Follow the Sankramana timing published by the Panchanga and Matha.
Temple worship, sharing food, and acts of charity are widely associated with the day.
Regional customs differ; family tradition remains the best guide.

title: Rathasaptami
subtitle: Magha Shukla Saptami
description: Ratha Saptami is the Magha Shukla Saptami observance for Surya. The Madhwa reference presents it as a day of early-morning worship, Surya arghya, and gratitude for the season and harvest.
notes: Those following the traditional practice begin with an early bath before sunrise.
The reference describes using seven arka leaves for the bath, followed by Sandhyavandana, Saligrama puja, and Surya worship.
Follow the SRS Matha or family procedure for mantras, offerings, and the exact timing.

title: Mahashivaratri
subtitle: The great night of Shiva
description: Mahashivaratri falls on Magha Krishna Chaturdashi. The Madhwa reference frames its observance through Hari dhyana and records a distinct sampradaya-specific qualification on fasting and jagarana.
notes: Offer worship in the form and timing followed by your family or local temple.
The Madhwa reference does not prescribe fasting or night vigil as a required procedure; if undertaken, it should be with Hari dhyana.
Follow SRS Matha guidance for the appropriate local observance.
